findings.where: First screen (hero), desktop and phone, and the whole page; the 'address strip' the palette and texture specimen both promise
findings.fault: The page has no way to reach Mark anywhere. The first screen has no action at all, and the email address is not shown. The parts map lists no mailto link or contact link, and the nav has no Contact item. The palette names pad yellow as 'the address strip', and the texture swatch draws a yellow band at the foot of the sheet, but no such strip is on the hero or anywhere else. So the one place the brief allows the legal-pad yellow, behind the contact panel, is missing too.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has read Mark's line and wants to write to him has nowhere to click and no address to copy. The founder's personal-advisor test needs 'one direct, personal way to reach him', and the brief's first screen needs 'one action with the address shown'. This page fails both, so it cannot do its one job.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download'
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque. That face is not in the stated type pair, which gives Newsreader 500 for subheads and Public Sans for labels. It is the loudest type on the article and jars against the light serif voice. It reads like a tech blog, not a legal journal.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for 'refined' and 'nothing in-your-face techy'. Angélique would also object: she copies the specimen when she adds subheads, and the page's own specification contradicts it.

findings.where: Motion sketch section, the full-width lavender panel (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The motion sketch sits on a saturated lavender field, a hue in no part of the palette. It is the most strongly coloured area below the fold. Blue linework and a blue link sit on it. It breaks the direction's 'one soft ground, house blue and grey the only ink'.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges whether the tile is built 'in or around' #0070C0 and #404040. A purple block suggests a palette the direction rules out and weakens the calm, paper-only character the tile claims.

findings.where: Article specimen title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' against the hero line
findings.fault: The article title is set in a heavy, bold serif. The hero line and the type pair use a light display cut. The two pages of one site read as two different typographic voices, and the specimen does not show how the stated 300-weight display holds on an article.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing homepage and article as one identity. A reader moving from the home page to an article meets a louder, blunter voice than Mark's line promised.

findings.fault: The four colour chips are four different shapes: a square-cornered box, a rounded box, an ellipse, and a box with a thick blue border that looks selected. Like parts are not treated alike, and the blue-bordered yellow chip borrows a 'selected' look.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the palette: the odd shapes and the highlighted yellow suggest meanings (a rank, a selection) the colours don't have.

findings.fault: The PDF's details ('Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF') sit pushed to the far right, away from the title they describe. The gap weakens their grouping with the link.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning the PDF list, which the brief calls 'the product': they have to track across the empty space to tie each date and format to its title.

findings.fault: At phone width the four-column table squeezes the 'Element' descriptions into one- or two-word lines that run down the panel. It reads as a ragged column of fragments.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reviewing the motion sketch on a phone: the timing is hard to follow and the section looks unfinished.
